subject: Tenant go-live safety & ops checklist - Acme Health
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant go-live safety & ops checklist - Acme Health

Jordan —

Thanks for the call earlier. As promised, here is our concise go-live safety checklist so we can align on day-one responsibilities and blockers. This is intentionally short so the Acme team can confirm quickly.

Actionable checklist (please reply with Y/N or a short note next to each item):

1) Network connectivity
   - BGP/peering established or VPN tunnel in place (include gateway IPs)
   - Egress IPs allowlisted for token exchange and telemetry (list attached)

2) Identity & access
   - Service account created with least-privilege keys (we recommend short-lived keys)
   - KMS access plan for model keys provided? (yes/no)

3) Domain naming & TLS
   - Certificate issuance in progress or certs uploaded to your vault

4) Smoke traffic plan
   - Time window for first test (2 hours) and expected RPS

5) Rollback & escalation
   - Primary contacts for the day and on-call rotation

Attachments: site network diagram, credentials handshake template, Redwood preflight checklist (v1.2).

If you can confirm items 1–3 by EOD Pacific we’ll lock the smoke window for tomorrow morning.

Cheers,

Dylan Brooks
Deployment Lead, Customer Onboarding
Redwood Inference

---
Note: internal ops copy to Karthik and Kimberly to pick up technical and procurement items respectively.

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>

Dylan —

Thanks, received. Quick answers inline below:  

1) Network connectivity — VPN tunnel is live; gateway IPs are 34.120.11.45 / 34.120.11.46. I attached the exported peering doc.

2) Identity & access — Service account exists; procurement needs to approve key rotation cadence. KMS: we manage keys in AWS KMS; need to confirm if Redwood requires raw key import or will use cross-account decrypt.

3) TLS — Certs are internal; we can provide a wildcard cert through your upload portal.

Smoke window: tomorrow 08/17 08:00–10:00 PT works for our infra team.

Jordan Lee
Cloud Engineering, Acme Health

Attachment: acme_peering_export.zip

Jordan / Dylan —

Quick tech notes from infra:  

- VPN IPs look good. We'll terminate NAT at our edge and expect Acme to route the two gateway IPs. Please confirm that the tunnel supports MTU 1400 for model payloads; small tokens plus chunks can exceed default limits.

- KMS: Redwood supports cross-account decrypt via KMS grants (preferred) or customer-managed HSM. We do NOT request raw key material. If Acme can create a KMS key and grant us decrypt-only permissions for the hosting account, that's the cleanest path.

- TLS: wildcard cert upload is fine; we will use the cert for internal api.<redacted>.acme.local endpoints. Please provide the cert + chain in PEM format.

Ben — looping you on the smoke plan; can your ops team stand by 07:45 PT tomorrow to flip traffic?

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Jordan —

Two procurement items before we ship:  

1) SOC2 evidence path: Please confirm if you need our SOC2 report or a scoped SOC2 letter for the VPC deployment. We can provide both; scoped letter is faster (24 hours).

2) Contract amendment: there's a small note around KMS and key custody in the attachment (redwood-kms-amendment-draft.docx). If procurement can review and sign, we can enable the cross-account decrypt grant sooner.

I've attached the amendment and our evidence checklist. Ben — can you prepare the runbook pages for the smoke test (short step-by-step) and share back by 3:30 PM PT?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-kms-amendment-draft.docx, redwood-evidence-checklist.pdf
